mr_title: Used unnest for bulk inserts on Postgres when possible.
mr_description:
This should make bulk_create significantly faster on Postgres when provided
only literal values.

Thanks James Sewell for writing about this technique, Tom Forbes for
validating the performance benefits, David Sanders and Mariusz Felisiak
for the review.

expected_issues.title: UNNEST cast to length-limited type silently truncates values
expected_issues.description:
The UNNEST bulk insert casts each column to field.db_type()[], e.g. varchar(50)[], and PostgreSQL silently truncates values when casting to a length-limited type, so over-long values are stored truncated instead of raising an error.

A regular INSERT of a 60-character string into varchar(50) raises 'value too long'. With the new strategy the values are first cast as `(%s)::varchar(50)[]`; an explicit cast to a length-limited character type truncates silently in PostgreSQL. bulk_create therefore loses data without error. The cast should use the base type without parameters (varchar[]), as was done for bulk_update (#33647).
